proof_dependency_chain: Fourier coefficient identity and irrationality yield uniqueness on zero-mean functions.
A polynomial divisor lower bound preserves rapid Fourier decay and constructs a smooth inverse.
Single Fourier modes and a weighted coefficient sum prove the exact Sobolev loss criterion in both directions.
Failure of every polynomial bound produces one fixed smooth forcing whose necessarily prescribed solution coefficients are unbounded.
The quadratic conjugate gives an attained one-derivative bound for sqrt(2)-1; Pell frequencies show every smaller nonnegative loss fails.
Integration by parts with m+4 derivatives leaves a summable cubic decay on the two-dimensional lattice and yields the required C^m estimate.
boundary_checks: All functions are complex-valued smooth functions on the exact unit-period torus, and both forcing and chosen solution have zero mean.
No finite derivative bound is assumed for arbitrary irrational alpha; nonresonance and tame inversion are separated.
The bad forcing is a single actual smooth function, not a family chosen after each estimate.
Sobolev estimates cover every real r and their constants are independent of u.
The exact arithmetic criterion retains endpoint information; the optional irrationality exponent is not an additional candidate obligation.
The minimum one-derivative claim concerns Sobolev norms; four is not claimed optimal for C^m norms.
The local source/formal estimate discrepancy does not refute the fixed-direction estimate or the global PDE theorem.
